context:
Goal: the project records stay short, and still protect your data.
Problem (rule): the compliance run flagged six lines that restrict Claude on a password, token, login or private datum, and only you can say which of them to prune.
Based on (read): the lines are CLAUDE.md lines 43, 83, 84 and 85, .claude/rules/sync.md line 46 and .claude/rules/photos.md line 11 on main; the coordinator changes none until you decide.
Departs from: main keeps all six lines — option b removes them from the records.
Waiting on: your answer; the compliance lanes run meanwhile.

lastAnswer.note: b: prune all six lines (saved in git).

options.gain: Nothing that guards your check-in data or the key is lost.
options.how: The coordinator changes nothing and tells the compliance run to leave these lines.
options.label: Keep all six lines
options.lose: Every session keeps reading six more lines on each turn.

options.gain: Every session reads six fewer lines on each turn.
options.how: The coordinator removes the six lines in one records change.
options.label: Prune all six lines
options.lose: A rule that keeps the key and token out of the shared origin is gone, so a lane could break it unseen.

reply: You picked b: prune all six lines (saved in git, 2026-11-22 12:27 CST). I passed it to the coordinator to remove them in one records change. 12:29 CST.
short: Compliance run: keep or prune six secret-related rule lines
title: Should the six rule lines about the device key, GitHub token and private data stay in the project records?
why: Unmeasured: keeping is the safe side, since the first line is a rule whose breaking costs months of data (my reading, not the coordinator's).
